title_options: Agent Memory Chunking: When Smaller Chunks Lose the Answer
Why Single-Fact Recall Hides a Chunking Failure in Agent Memory
Chunk Size for Agent Memory: Fine Chunks Split Two-Fact Answers
presentation.title_rationale: Selected title fronts the topic (agent memory chunking) and the reader's consequence instead of the method. 'When smaller chunks lose the answer' is exactly what Result 2 measures: two-fact hit@1 falls from 13/15 with whole-document vectors to 0/15 at 3-sentence and single-sentence chunks, while Result 1 shows single-fact recall is unchanged. The conditional 'when' keeps it honest, and the fixture, three embedders and 2026 date that made the old headline unreadable are in the introduction and method section. 58 characters, so no long_title_reason is needed.
presentation.visual_purpose: Conceptual checklist of the mechanism the article measures: a question needs two facts, the chunk boundaries decide whether those facts can arrive in one retrieved unit, and the retrieved evidence can therefore hold only half the answer. It is labelled 'conceptual checklist - not new measurement data' and carries no numbers, so its scope is the Result 2 mechanism at k=1 only, not the measured hit@1 counts.
